newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends down, Sammi trouble adds to woes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends down, Sammi trouble adds to woes.

text.p: The won ended Wednesday lower against the U.S. unit, propelled by concerns that Sammi Group's woes would lead to a further tightening of overseas credit to domestic companies and reduce dollar supplies, dealers said.
Sammi Steel and four other affiliates filed for court receivership late Tuesday as they have been reeling under the weight of debts and accumulating corporate losses.
The won closed the day at a low of 884.80, compared to Tuesday's close of 883.10. It opened trading at a high of 883.60.
"Sammi is definitely one of the factors behind the won's weakness today," said a European bank dealer.
Other factors pressuring the won is the nation's mounting trade deficit, the dollar's strength against the Japanese yen on world markets, and foreigners pulling out of the local stock market.
The central bank did not intervene in spot trading on Wednesday, but was seen offering to sell $30 million dollars each at 897.50 won in three-month and 912.00 won in six-month forward trading.
The central bank has refused to comment on talk of its intervention on the interbank market.
Dealers said they expected the central bank to step into the spot market on Thursday, if the won fell below the 885 mark.
"But many players are waiting for the central bank to intervene because it's a good opportunity to buy dollars," the European bank dealer said.
The base mid-rate for Thursday was seen at 884.40, against 882.60 on Wednesday.
